pr.title: FIX: proper handling of group memberships

raw_findings.body: totalPages reports one page too many (e.g. 2 pages for 50 members). showingLast stays false on the real last page, so the 'next' link remains enabled; clicking it sets offset = user_count and findMembers loads an empty member page, showing '2/2' (or 'N/N') with no members.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Pagination controls expose a phantom empty final page and mislabel the total page count in the admin group member list.
raw_findings.impact: totalPages reports one page too many (e.g. 2 pages for 50 members). showingLast stays false on the real last page, so the 'next' link remains enabled; clicking it sets offset = user_count and findMembers loads an empty member page, showing '2/2' (or 'N/N') with no members.
raw_findings.root_cause: Page count computed as floor(count/limit)+1, which over-counts by one whenever count is evenly divisible by limit.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute total pages with ceiling division, e.g. `return Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"));`, instead of floor(...) + 1.
raw_findings.title: totalPages off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
raw_findings.trigger: View an admin group whose user_count is an exact multiple of the page limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50, or 100 with limit 50).

raw_findings.body: group.add pushes a duplicate GroupUser through the has_many :through association: either a unique-index violation raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and the request 500s with no user-facing error, or a duplicate membership row is created and user_count is inflated.
raw_findings.evidence:
usernames.split(",").each do |username|
      if user = User.find_by_username(username)
        group.add(user)
      end
    end
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled duplicate-membership insert causes a 500 response or corrupted membership/user_count data instead of a graceful no-op.
raw_findings.impact: group.add pushes a duplicate GroupUser through the has_many :through association: either a unique-index violation raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and the request 500s with no user-facing error, or a duplicate membership row is created and user_count is inflated.
raw_findings.root_cause: New add_members endpoint calls Group#add (users.push) unconditionally without checking existing membership.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Skip users who are already members before calling group.add (e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)`), or rescue/validate duplicate membership and return a clean error.
raw_findings.title: add_members adds users already in the group without a membership check
raw_findings.trigger: Admin submits a username that is already a member of the group via the new PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members endpoint (easy since the input is not cleared after a successful add and can be resubmitted).

raw_findings.body: The previous removal path (Group#usernames= plus the destroy_deletions after_save hook) explicitly ran `update_all 'primary_group_id = NULL'` for removed users; the replacement endpoint uses association delete which bypasses that cleanup, leaving users with a stale primary_group_id referencing a group they no longer belong to (wrong badges/flair, inconsistent data).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent data inconsistency: removed members retain the group as their primary group.
raw_findings.impact: The previous removal path (Group#usernames= plus the destroy_deletions after_save hook) explicitly ran `update_all 'primary_group_id = NULL'` for removed users; the replacement endpoint uses association delete which bypasses that cleanup, leaving users with a stale primary_group_id referencing a group they no longer belong to (wrong badges/flair, inconsistent data).
raw_findings.root_cause: The new remove_member endpoint replaces the usernames= diff flow but omits the primary_group_id cleanup that flow performed in destroy_deletions.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After deleting the membership, null out primary_group_id for the removed user (e.g. reuse Group#remove or run `User.where(id: user_id, primary_group_id: group.id).update_all(primary_group_id: nil)`).
raw_findings.title: remove_member deletes join rows without clearing users' primary_group_id
raw_findings.trigger: Admin removes a member whose primary_group_id points at this group via the new DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members endpoint.

raw_findings.body: PostgreSQL rejects negative OFFSET/LIMIT values ('OFFSET must not be negative'), so the request raises and returns a 500 instead of a 400 or a clamped page; previously non-automatic groups never hit this code path.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Crafted query-string parameters produce server errors on a public endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: PostgreSQL rejects negative OFFSET/LIMIT values ('OFFSET must not be negative'), so the request raises and returns a 500 instead of a 400 or a clamped page; previously non-automatic groups never hit this code path.
raw_findings.root_cause: New pagination code trusts raw request params for limit/offset without clamping to non-negative values.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Clamp the params before querying, e.g. `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max` and bound limit to a sane positive range.
raw_findings.title: members endpoint passes unvalidated offset/limit params straight into SQL
raw_findings.trigger: A client calls GET /groups/:group_id/members.json with offset=-1 (or limit=-2), which the new always-paginated code path forwards directly to .limit()/.offset().

raw_findings.body: The breaking response-format change and the now-universal limit/offset behavior of GroupsController#members ship untested; the pending spec would fail if ever enabled, and regressions in total/limit/offset math would go undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested public API contract change; stale pending test asserts the removed format.
raw_findings.impact: The breaking response-format change and the now-universal limit/offset behavior of GroupsController#members ship untested; the pending spec would fail if ever enabled, and regressions in total/limit/offset math would go undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: Patch rewrote the members action's response contract and pagination semantics without adding or updating any spec for it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb: un-pend and rewrite the pagination example against the new {members, meta} format, asserting total, limit, and offset values.
raw_findings.title: Changed members.json response shape has no controller spec coverage and stale pending spec
raw_findings.trigger: Running the suite after this patch: spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb still contains only the old pending pagination example that parses the body as a flat array (`members = JSON.parse(response.body); members.map{ |m| m['username'] }`), which no longer matches the new {members:, meta:} envelope, and no active spec asserts the new pagination/meta behavior.

raw_findings.body: The same usernames are resubmitted to the add_members endpoint, which has no duplicate-membership guard, producing a server error or duplicate membership rows; the shipped TODO comment shows the incomplete behavior was known but not fixed before merge.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale form state enables accidental duplicate submissions of the same member list.
raw_findings.impact: The same usernames are resubmitted to the add_members endpoint, which has no duplicate-membership guard, producing a server error or duplicate membership rows; the shipped TODO comment shows the incomplete behavior was known but not fixed before merge.
raw_findings.root_cause: The addMembers action was merged with an acknowledged TODO instead of resetting the bound usernames value after submission.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Clear the usernames property (e.g. `this.set("usernames", null)`) after a successful addMembers call instead of leaving the TODO.
raw_findings.title: addMembers leaves entered usernames in the input after submitting
raw_findings.trigger: Admin adds members, then clicks the Add button again (the previously entered usernames are still populated in the user-selector).

validated_findings.trigger: Running the suite after this patch: spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb still contains only the old pending pagination example that parses the body as a flat array (`members = JSON.parse(response.body); members.map{ |m| m['username'] }`), which no longer matches the new {members:, meta:} envelope, and no active spec asserts the new pagination/meta behavior.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage observation, not a defect in the patch code itself. The pending spec at line 72-85 in groups_controller_spec.rb is pre-existing and marked pending. While the response format changed, absence of test coverage is a quality concern, not a bug introduced by the patch. The claim is about missing tests rather than incorrect behavior.

validated_findings.body: The same usernames are resubmitted to the add_members endpoint, which has no duplicate-membership guard, producing a server error or duplicate membership rows; the shipped TODO comment shows the incomplete behavior was known but not fixed before merge.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale form state enables accidental duplicate submissions of the same member list.
validated_findings.impact: The same usernames are resubmitted to the add_members endpoint, which has no duplicate-membership guard, producing a server error or duplicate membership rows; the shipped TODO comment shows the incomplete behavior was known but not fixed before merge.
validated_findings.root_cause: The addMembers action was merged with an acknowledged TODO instead of resetting the bound usernames value after submission.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Clear the usernames property (e.g. `this.set("usernames", null)`) after a successful addMembers call instead of leaving the TODO.
validated_findings.title: addMembers leaves entered usernames in the input after submitting
validated_findings.trigger: Admin adds members, then clicks the Add button again (the previously entered usernames are still populated in the user-selector).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The TODO comment at line 62 and the fact that usernames aren't cleared is acknowledged behavior, not a hidden bug. The duplicate submission issue depends on candidate 1's claim about add_members failing on duplicates, which is unsubstantiated. The input not being cleared is a UX issue explicitly marked as TODO, not an unintended defect.
